summary: 41-year-old driver after a frontal collision: severe dyspnoea, SpO₂ 84 % on oxygen, RR 36, HR 138, BP 80/50, trachea deviated to the left, absent breath sounds and hyper-resonance on the right, distended neck veins.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Chest injury in car crash, cannot breathe
inputs.hpi: Driver in a frontal collision 20 minutes ago, struck the steering wheel. Right chest pain and rapidly worsening breathlessness in the ambulance.

exam.general: Agitated, cyanosed. RR 36, SpO2 84% on 15 L, HR 138, BP 80/50. Distended neck veins.
exam.respiratory: Trachea deviated to the left. Absent breath sounds and hyper-resonant percussion over the right hemithorax. Surgical emphysema right chest wall. Tension pneumothorax clinically.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Tension pneumothorax (right, traumatic)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Right tension pneumothorax after blunt chest trauma — clinical diagnosis. Immediate decompression without imaging, then chest drain.

redFlags.note: The engine must name tension physiology, not only "pneumothorax".

mustExclude.note: ATLS 10 moved adult needle decompression to the 4th/5th intercostal space anterior to the mid-axillary line (chest wall too thick at the 2nd ICS mid-clavicular line in many adults). Surgeon to confirm the site the practice teaches.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Change the adult site to the 4th/5th ICS just anterior to the mid-axillary line (2nd ICS MCL for children); surgeon to confirm.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — thoracic trauma
guideline.section: Chapter 4: tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis treated by immediate decompression without waiting for imaging; in adults needle decompression at the 4th/5th intercostal space anterior to the mid-axillary line (2nd ICS mid-clavicular line remains acceptable in children), followed by chest tube
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 4.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — initial assessment and management
guideline.section: Chapter 1: primary survey in order — control of exsanguinating external haemorrhage, airway with cervical spine restriction, breathing, circulation with haemorrhage control, disability, exposure (x/c-ABCDE); adjuncts (FAST, CXR, pelvic XR); resuscitation before definitive imaging in unstable patients
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 1.

rationale: Clinical tension pneumothorax with obstructive shock. ATLS 10: clinical diagnosis, immediate decompression without waiting for imaging; adult site 4th/5th ICS anterior to the mid-axillary line. Tests recognition, the decompression step and the recommended site.
